lessons.title: Service managers
lessons.summary: A service manager supervises processes and coordinates their lifecycle with system dependencies.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A service manager supervises processes and coordinates their lifecycle with system dependencies.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: systemd represents services and other resources as units. Start order, readiness and restart policies are separate settings. A process running does not necessarily mean its application is ready to serve traffic.

lessons.takeaway: systemd represents services and other resources as units. Start order, readiness and restart policies are separate settings. A process running does not necessarily mean its application is ready to serve traffic.

lessons.title: Enable versus start
lessons.summary: Starting a service activates it now; enabling arranges activation through configured boot or target relationships.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Starting a service activates it now; enabling arranges activation through configured boot or target relationships.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A service can be enabled but stopped, or running but disabled. Check both states when diagnosing reboot-only failures. Some static units are activated by dependencies or sockets and are not directly enabled.

lessons.takeaway: A service can be enabled but stopped, or running but disabled. Check both states when diagnosing reboot-only failures. Some static units are activated by dependencies or sockets and are not directly enabled.

lessons.title: Unit overrides
lessons.summary: Unit drop-ins customize packaged systemd units without editing vendor files.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Unit drop-ins customize packaged systemd units without editing vendor files.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The manager combines the base unit and overrides. After editing, daemon-reload refreshes unit definitions; a service restart or reload may still be needed to apply runtime changes. Use systemctl cat to inspect the effective sources.

lessons.takeaway: The manager combines the base unit and overrides. After editing, daemon-reload refreshes unit definitions; a service restart or reload may still be needed to apply runtime changes. Use systemctl cat to inspect the effective sources.

lessons.title: Journals
lessons.summary: The systemd journal collects structured service and system log entries.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: The systemd journal collects structured service and system log entries.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Filter by unit, boot and time range to align evidence with an incident. Retention and persistent storage settings determine what survives reboot. Empty results can reflect filtering or retention rather than absence of a failure.

lessons.takeaway: Filter by unit, boot and time range to align evidence with an incident. Retention and persistent storage settings determine what survives reboot. Empty results can reflect filtering or retention rather than absence of a failure.

lessons.title: Accounts
lessons.summary: System accounts bind numeric user and group identities to ownership and authorization rules.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: System accounts bind numeric user and group identities to ownership and authorization rules.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Services should use dedicated identities with limited access. Directory permissions, supplementary groups and login policies affect what those identities can do. Removing an account does not automatically reassign every file owned by its old UID.

lessons.takeaway: Services should use dedicated identities with limited access. Directory permissions, supplementary groups and login policies affect what those identities can do. Removing an account does not automatically reassign every file owned by its old UID.

lessons.title: SSH keys
lessons.summary: SSH public-key authentication proves possession of a private key without sending that key to the server.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: SSH public-key authentication proves possession of a private key without sending that key to the server.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The server checks authorized keys and policy; the client separately verifies the server's host identity. Restrict key access and rotate compromised credentials. A trusted user key does not remove the need to verify the host key.

lessons.takeaway: The server checks authorized keys and policy; the client separately verifies the server's host identity. Restrict key access and rotate compromised credentials. A trusted user key does not remove the need to verify the host key.

lessons.title: Package management
lessons.summary: A package manager installs versioned software and tracks dependencies and package-owned files.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A package manager installs versioned software and tracks dependencies and package-owned files.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Use trusted repositories and understand distribution-specific update behavior. Installation success does not prove running processes use patched code. Plan service restarts and verify versions and health after maintenance.

lessons.takeaway: Use trusted repositories and understand distribution-specific update behavior. Installation success does not prove running processes use patched code. Plan service restarts and verify versions and health after maintenance.

lessons.title: Scheduled jobs
lessons.summary: Schedulers execute recurring or delayed tasks through cron, timers or other job systems.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Schedulers execute recurring or delayed tasks through cron, timers or other job systems.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Jobs often run with a different environment and working directory from an interactive shell. Define absolute paths, output handling, locking and timeout behavior. Test overlapping runs and missed-run semantics rather than relying on the calendar expression alone.

lessons.takeaway: Jobs often run with a different environment and working directory from an interactive shell. Define absolute paths, output handling, locking and timeout behavior. Test overlapping runs and missed-run semantics rather than relying on the calendar expression alone.

lessons.title: Time synchronization
lessons.summary: Clock synchronization aligns system wall time with trusted time sources.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Clock synchronization aligns system wall time with trusted time sources.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Accurate time supports certificate validation, logs and distributed coordination. Inspect source selection and offset rather than only whether the daemon runs. Applications should still use monotonic clocks for elapsed durations.

lessons.takeaway: Accurate time supports certificate validation, logs and distributed coordination. Inspect source selection and offset rather than only whether the daemon runs. Applications should still use monotonic clocks for elapsed durations.

lessons.title: Disk layout
lessons.summary: Disk layout describes devices, partitions, logical volumes, filesystems and their mount points.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Disk layout describes devices, partitions, logical volumes, filesystems and their mount points.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: These layers have separate sizes and identities. Expanding a cloud disk may still require partition, logical-volume and filesystem expansion. Use stable identifiers and confirm the exact target before modifying storage.

lessons.takeaway: These layers have separate sizes and identities. Expanding a cloud disk may still require partition, logical-volume and filesystem expansion. Use stable identifiers and confirm the exact target before modifying storage.

lessons.title: Log rotation
lessons.summary: Log rotation bounds log-file growth by renaming, compressing or expiring older data.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Log rotation bounds log-file growth by renaming, compressing or expiring older data.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Applications may need a signal or reopen operation after rotation because open descriptors continue referencing old files. Copy-truncate has race and data-loss trade-offs. Match retention to capacity and investigation needs.

lessons.takeaway: Applications may need a signal or reopen operation after rotation because open descriptors continue referencing old files. Copy-truncate has race and data-loss trade-offs. Match retention to capacity and investigation needs.

lessons.title: Backups
lessons.summary: A backup preserves a recoverable copy of data and required metadata outside the active failure domain.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A backup preserves a recoverable copy of data and required metadata outside the active failure domain.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Choose schedules and retention from recovery objectives. Protect encryption keys and credentials separately from the failing system. Replication alone is insufficient when it quickly copies deletion, corruption or malicious changes.

lessons.takeaway: Choose schedules and retention from recovery objectives. Protect encryption keys and credentials separately from the failing system. Replication alone is insufficient when it quickly copies deletion, corruption or malicious changes.

lessons.title: Restore verification
lessons.summary: Restore verification tests that a backup can produce a complete and usable system.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Restore verification tests that a backup can produce a complete and usable system.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Restore into an isolated target, validate integrity and execute representative application reads or transactions. Record data age and elapsed recovery time. A checksum validates bytes but does not prove application consistency or dependency availability.

lessons.takeaway: Restore into an isolated target, validate integrity and execute representative application reads or transactions. Record data age and elapsed recovery time. A checksum validates bytes but does not prove application consistency or dependency availability.

lessons.title: RAID
lessons.summary: RAID combines disks to provide selected performance or device-failure tolerance properties.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: RAID combines disks to provide selected performance or device-failure tolerance properties.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Different levels have different capacity and failure trade-offs. Rebuilds increase load and may expose additional disk failures. RAID does not protect against accidental deletion, application corruption or loss of the entire system.

lessons.takeaway: Different levels have different capacity and failure trade-offs. Rebuilds increase load and may expose additional disk failures. RAID does not protect against accidental deletion, application corruption or loss of the entire system.

lessons.title: LVM
lessons.summary: Logical Volume Manager pools block devices and allocates logical volumes from volume groups.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Logical Volume Manager pools block devices and allocates logical volumes from volume groups.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Physical volumes supply extents; logical volumes consume them and may host filesystems. Extending a logical volume and growing its filesystem are distinct steps. Shrinking support and order depend on the filesystem and need careful planning.

lessons.takeaway: Physical volumes supply extents; logical volumes consume them and may host filesystems. Extending a logical volume and growing its filesystem are distinct steps. Shrinking support and order depend on the filesystem and need careful planning.

lessons.title: Filesystem mounts
lessons.summary: Mounting makes a filesystem accessible at a path in the directory tree.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Mounting makes a filesystem accessible at a path in the directory tree.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Persistent definitions commonly use UUIDs in fstab or mount units. A missing mount can cause an application to write into the underlying root filesystem directory. Confirm source, options and dependencies before starting storage-dependent services.

lessons.takeaway: Persistent definitions commonly use UUIDs in fstab or mount units. A missing mount can cause an application to write into the underlying root filesystem directory. Confirm source, options and dependencies before starting storage-dependent services.

lessons.title: Boot recovery
lessons.summary: Boot recovery diagnoses failures in firmware, bootloader, kernel, initramfs, mounts or service startup.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Boot recovery diagnoses failures in firmware, bootloader, kernel, initramfs, mounts or service startup.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Locate the failing stage and use the distribution's rescue workflow. A bad fstab entry and a missing storage driver require different fixes. Preserve console access and a known-good boot option before changing critical configuration.

lessons.takeaway: Locate the failing stage and use the distribution's rescue workflow. A bad fstab entry and a missing storage driver require different fixes. Preserve console access and a known-good boot option before changing critical configuration.

lessons.title: Patching
lessons.summary: Patching updates software to address defects or vulnerabilities under a controlled rollout.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Patching updates software to address defects or vulnerabilities under a controlled rollout.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Identify affected running components, test compatibility and define rollback or forward recovery. Apply to a small cohort first, then verify service behavior before broader rollout. Reboot requirements depend on the changed components and update mechanism.

lessons.takeaway: Identify affected running components, test compatibility and define rollback or forward recovery. Apply to a small cohort first, then verify service behavior before broader rollout. Reboot requirements depend on the changed components and update mechanism.

lessons.title: Configuration drift
lessons.summary: Configuration drift is divergence between intended configuration and actual system state.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Configuration drift is divergence between intended configuration and actual system state.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Compare effective settings, package versions and manual changes with the declared baseline. Decide whether an emergency change should be adopted or reverted. Blindly restoring a baseline during an incident can undo a necessary mitigation.

lessons.takeaway: Compare effective settings, package versions and manual changes with the declared baseline. Decide whether an emergency change should be adopted or reverted. Blindly restoring a baseline during an incident can undo a necessary mitigation.

lessons.title: Access reviews
lessons.summary: Access reviews check that current privileges still match current responsibilities.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Access reviews check that current privileges still match current responsibilities.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Include local groups, sudo rules, SSH keys, service identities and emergency access. Remove stale grants through a controlled process and verify a supported administration path remains. An inventory of accounts alone misses delegated privileges.

lessons.takeaway: Include local groups, sudo rules, SSH keys, service identities and emergency access. Remove stale grants through a controlled process and verify a supported administration path remains. An inventory of accounts alone misses delegated privileges.

lessons.title: Sudo policy
lessons.summary: Sudo policy determines which users may execute which commands as another identity.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Sudo policy determines which users may execute which commands as another identity.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Command paths, arguments and environment handling influence the scope of a grant. An allowed shell or editable script may effectively grant unrestricted privilege. Validate policy syntax before installing it and inspect effective rights.

lessons.takeaway: Command paths, arguments and environment handling influence the scope of a grant. An allowed shell or editable script may effectively grant unrestricted privilege. Validate policy syntax before installing it and inspect effective rights.

lessons.title: Resource limits
lessons.summary: Resource limits bound process or service consumption such as descriptors, tasks, memory and CPU.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Resource limits bound process or service consumption such as descriptors, tasks, memory and CPU.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Shell limits and service-manager settings can differ. Inspect the limits on the actual running process, not just the login shell. Raise a limit only after distinguishing legitimate demand from leaks or unbounded concurrency.

lessons.takeaway: Shell limits and service-manager settings can differ. Inspect the limits on the actual running process, not just the login shell. Raise a limit only after distinguishing legitimate demand from leaks or unbounded concurrency.

lessons.title: System monitoring
lessons.summary: System monitoring measures host health, saturation and service behavior over time.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: System monitoring measures host health, saturation and service behavior over time.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Correlate CPU, memory, storage, network and application signals during the same interval. A current healthy snapshot may miss an earlier spike. Use baselines and historical trends to separate expected workload from regression.

lessons.takeaway: Correlate CPU, memory, storage, network and application signals during the same interval. A current healthy snapshot may miss an earlier spike. Use baselines and historical trends to separate expected workload from regression.

lessons.title: Immutable hosts
lessons.summary: Immutable infrastructure replaces hosts from a defined image instead of accumulating in-place changes.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Immutable infrastructure replaces hosts from a defined image instead of accumulating in-place changes.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Store durable data outside replaceable instances and automate bootstrapping. An image version makes rollback clearer, but external schemas and state may still require migration compatibility. Emergency edits should be captured in the image definition.

lessons.takeaway: Store durable data outside replaceable instances and automate bootstrapping. An image version makes rollback clearer, but external schemas and state may still require migration compatibility. Emergency edits should be captured in the image definition.

lessons.title: Capacity forecasts
lessons.summary: Capacity forecasting estimates when demand will exceed usable resource headroom.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Capacity forecasting estimates when demand will exceed usable resource headroom.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Use growth trends, seasonality, procurement delay and failure reserve. Track the actual bottleneck rather than extrapolating CPU alone. Revisit forecasts after major workload or architecture changes.

lessons.takeaway: Use growth trends, seasonality, procurement delay and failure reserve. Track the actual bottleneck rather than extrapolating CPU alone. Revisit forecasts after major workload or architecture changes.

lessons.title: Remote administration
lessons.summary: Remote administration provides controlled access to systems without local console interaction.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Remote administration provides controlled access to systems without local console interaction.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Maintain a tested emergency path, protect authentication and confirm the target before changes. For network or SSH changes, preserve an existing session until a separate new login succeeds. Otherwise a small configuration error can lock out responders.

lessons.takeaway: Maintain a tested emergency path, protect authentication and confirm the target before changes. For network or SSH changes, preserve an existing session until a separate new login succeeds. Otherwise a small configuration error can lock out responders.

lessons.title: Data sanitization
lessons.summary: Data sanitization makes retired storage data unrecoverable to the required assurance level.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Data sanitization makes retired storage data unrecoverable to the required assurance level.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Methods depend on medium, encryption design and threat model. File deletion or formatting is not equivalent to secure erasure, especially with snapshots and SSD wear leveling. Track backup copies and key disposal as part of retirement.

lessons.takeaway: Methods depend on medium, encryption design and threat model. File deletion or formatting is not equivalent to secure erasure, especially with snapshots and SSD wear leveling. Track backup copies and key disposal as part of retirement.

lessons.title: Fleet changes
lessons.summary: Fleet changes apply a configuration or software update across multiple machines.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Fleet changes apply a configuration or software update across multiple machines.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Use canary groups, bounded batches and health gates. Separate failure domains so one bad change does not remove all capacity at once. Stop automatically when error thresholds or health checks fail.

lessons.takeaway: Use canary groups, bounded batches and health gates. Separate failure domains so one bad change does not remove all capacity at once. Stop automatically when error thresholds or health checks fail.

lessons.title: Disaster documentation
lessons.summary: Disaster documentation records how to restore a service when normal systems or personnel are unavailable.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Disaster documentation records how to restore a service when normal systems or personnel are unavailable.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Include dependency order, recovery locations, credential retrieval and validation steps. Keep an accessible protected copy outside the affected environment. Test whether someone unfamiliar with the system can follow it.

lessons.takeaway: Include dependency order, recovery locations, credential retrieval and validation steps. Keep an accessible protected copy outside the affected environment. Test whether someone unfamiliar with the system can follow it.

lessons.title: Change verification
lessons.summary: Change verification confirms both the intended result and continued service health.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Change verification confirms both the intended result and continued service health.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Compare pre-change and post-change evidence, including user-facing behavior and dependency metrics. A zero exit code only confirms a command's own success conditions. Keep rollback criteria explicit until the observation window passes.

lessons.takeaway: Compare pre-change and post-change evidence, including user-facing behavior and dependency metrics. A zero exit code only confirms a command's own success conditions. Keep rollback criteria explicit until the observation window passes.

commands.title: Service state
commands.definition: Summarizes a systemd service's state and recent messages.
commands.purpose: Check whether startup failed, exited or remains active.
commands.environment: Replace APP with the actual unit; read-only inspection.
commands.interpretation: Loaded describes the unit definition; Active describes current state; Main PID identifies the process.
commands.safety: Replace APP with the actual unit; read-only inspection.

commands.title: Effective unit
commands.definition: Prints the unit file and drop-in configuration.
commands.purpose: Find overrides or unexpected startup arguments.
commands.environment: Read-only; displayed configuration may contain sensitive environment values.
commands.interpretation: File headers identify each source; later applicable overrides modify the base definition.
commands.safety: Read-only; displayed configuration may contain sensitive environment values.

commands.title: Service journal
commands.definition: Filters journal entries by service and recent time.
commands.purpose: Correlate startup failures with a change.
commands.environment: Read-only; redact secrets before sharing logs.
commands.interpretation: Read timestamps, process identifiers and errors together; retention can remove older evidence.
commands.safety: Read-only; redact secrets before sharing logs.

commands.title: Boot failures
commands.definition: Shows error-priority messages from the current boot.
commands.purpose: Narrow boot and initialization problems.
commands.environment: Read-only; inspect a broader priority range if necessary.
commands.interpretation: -b selects the boot and -p err includes error and more severe priorities; warnings are excluded.
commands.safety: Read-only; inspect a broader priority range if necessary.

commands.title: Failed units
commands.definition: Lists units currently in failed state.
commands.purpose: Find failed dependencies after reboot or maintenance.
commands.environment: Read-only; a previously recovered failure may no longer appear.
commands.interpretation: UNIT names the failed object; ACTIVE and SUB describe its state.
commands.safety: Read-only; a previously recovered failure may no longer appear.

commands.title: Timer schedule
commands.definition: Lists systemd timers and their recent and next triggers.
commands.purpose: Diagnose jobs that run late or not at all.
commands.environment: Read-only; inspect the activated service's logs to verify job success.
commands.expectedOutput: NEXT LEFT LAST PASSED UNIT ACTIVATES
commands.interpretation: NEXT and LEFT show expected scheduling; LAST and PASSED show prior activation; ACTIVATES names the target unit.
commands.safety: Read-only; inspect the activated service's logs to verify job success.

commands.title: Clock status
commands.definition: Displays system clock, timezone and synchronization status.
commands.purpose: Check clock assumptions during TLS or log-order problems.
commands.environment: Read-only; command availability depends on the host's service stack.
commands.interpretation: System clock synchronized and NTP service are different indicators; inspect the time source for detailed offset.
commands.safety: Read-only; command availability depends on the host's service stack.

commands.title: Storage layers
commands.definition: Lists block-device hierarchy and selected properties.
commands.purpose: Distinguish disk, partition and filesystem sizes before expansion.
commands.environment: Read-only; MOUNTPOINTS support depends on util-linux version.
commands.interpretation: Indented children belong to parent devices; a filesystem can be smaller than the underlying block device.
commands.safety: Read-only; MOUNTPOINTS support depends on util-linux version.

commands.title: Mount validation
commands.definition: Checks filesystem-table parsing and usability assumptions.
commands.purpose: Find fstab problems before a reboot.
commands.environment: Read-only verification; visibility and device availability affect results.
commands.expectedOutput: Success, no errors or warnings detected
commands.interpretation: Warnings and errors identify entries requiring investigation; success does not simulate every boot dependency.
commands.safety: Read-only verification; visibility and device availability affect results.

commands.title: SSH configuration check
commands.definition: Validates sshd configuration and host-key sanity.
commands.purpose: Catch syntax errors before reloading remote access.
commands.environment: May require elevated read access; validation alone does not prove a new login will succeed.
commands.interpretation: No output and zero exit status normally indicate validation success; errors name the problematic setting.
commands.safety: May require elevated read access; validation alone does not prove a new login will succeed.

commands.title: Log rotation preview
commands.definition: Parses rotation policy and explains planned decisions without rotating logs.
commands.purpose: Diagnose wrong paths, retention and rotation timing.
commands.environment: Debug mode does not update state or rotate files; output may include filesystem details.
commands.interpretation: Look for the selected log, last rotation and whether rotation is due.
commands.safety: Debug mode does not update state or rotate files; output may include filesystem details.

commands.title: Sudo syntax check
commands.definition: Checks installed sudoers policy syntax.
commands.purpose: Verify privilege-policy integrity before ending an administrative session.
commands.environment: Read-only check, usually requires privileged access; keep a working recovery session during policy edits.
commands.interpretation: Parsed OK identifies accepted files; line errors identify syntax faults.
commands.safety: Read-only check, usually requires privileged access; keep a working recovery session during policy edits.

commands.title: Effective unit properties
commands.command: systemctl show APP.service -p MainPID -p ActiveState -p SubState -p ExecMainStatus
commands.definition: Displays selected runtime properties for a systemd unit.
commands.purpose: Read machine-oriented evidence of process state and exit status.
commands.environment: Read-only; a live PID can still serve failed requests.
commands.interpretation: MainPID is the tracked process; ActiveState/SubState describe unit state. ExecMainStatus is not an HTTP health result.
commands.safety: Read-only; a live PID can still serve failed requests.

commands.title: Boot enablement
commands.definition: Reports whether unit installation relationships enable activation.
commands.purpose: Investigate why a manually started service does not return after boot.
commands.environment: Read-only; enablement does not mean currently running.
commands.interpretation: enabled, disabled, static and masked have different meanings; static units may start through dependencies.
commands.safety: Read-only; enablement does not mean currently running.

commands.title: Unit dependencies
commands.definition: Lists unit dependencies known to the manager.
commands.purpose: Inspect the activation relationships of a service.
commands.environment: Read-only; use unit properties to inspect ordering details when needed.
commands.interpretation: Tree structure shows related units; activation dependencies differ from explicit ordering constraints.
commands.safety: Read-only; use unit properties to inspect ordering details when needed.

commands.title: Reload manager configuration
commands.definition: Reloads unit definitions and regenerates the manager dependency view.
commands.purpose: Make edited unit files or drop-ins visible to systemd.
commands.environment: Changes the manager's configuration view. Validate unit edits and use the separate intended service action afterward.
commands.interpretation: Success is normally silent; it does not itself restart the service or reload application configuration.
commands.safety: Changes the manager's configuration view. Validate unit edits and use the separate intended service action afterward.

commands.title: Reload application configuration
commands.definition: Requests the unit's configured reload operation.
commands.purpose: Activate a supported application configuration change without a full restart.
commands.environment: Mutates application state and requires unit reload support. Validate configuration before invoking.
commands.interpretation: A successful job means the reload command completed; verify actual loaded configuration and service behavior.
commands.safety: Mutates application state and requires unit reload support. Validate configuration before invoking.

commands.title: Controlled service restart
commands.definition: Stops and starts a unit according to its configuration.
commands.purpose: Apply an approved change that requires a new process.
commands.environment: Disrupts a workload; verify dependency impact, capacity and recovery access first.
commands.interpretation: Successful exit indicates the start job completed under unit semantics; inspect logs and endpoint health afterward.
commands.safety: Disrupts a workload; verify dependency impact, capacity and recovery access first.

commands.title: Enable a service
commands.definition: Creates installation links according to the unit's Install section.
commands.purpose: Configure intended activation relationships such as boot startup.
commands.environment: Mutates host activation policy; inspect the unit and intended target first.
commands.interpretation: Created symlink messages identify changed links. This command without --now does not start the unit.
commands.safety: Mutates host activation policy; inspect the unit and intended target first.

commands.title: Historical boot logs
commands.definition: Lists boots represented in the journal.
commands.purpose: Find the boot index or ID for a failure before a reboot.
commands.environment: Read-only; availability depends on journal persistence and retention.
commands.interpretation: 0 is the current boot; negative offsets refer to earlier retained boots. Start/end timestamps delimit retained evidence.
commands.safety: Read-only; availability depends on journal persistence and retention.

commands.title: Previous boot errors
commands.definition: Reads warning-and-higher-priority entries from the previous retained boot.
commands.purpose: Investigate why a host failed before it restarted.
commands.environment: Read-only; log content may be sensitive and should be shared selectively.
commands.interpretation: -b -1 selects the prior boot; -p warning includes more severe priorities. Missing records may reflect retention limits.
commands.safety: Read-only; log content may be sensitive and should be shared selectively.

commands.title: Journal disk usage
commands.definition: Reports disk space used by journal files.
commands.purpose: Assess whether journaling contributes to filesystem pressure.
commands.environment: Read-only; inspect retention policy before deleting evidence.
commands.expectedOutput: Archived and active journals take up 1.2G in the file system.
commands.interpretation: The total describes journal storage, not all logs under /var/log.
commands.safety: Read-only; inspect retention policy before deleting evidence.

commands.title: User scheduled tasks
commands.definition: Lists the current user's cron entries.
commands.purpose: Compare scheduler command paths, timing and environment assumptions.
commands.environment: Read-only; inspect the correct account. System timers and /etc/cron* are separate sources.
commands.interpretation: Each non-comment entry begins with schedule fields followed by the command; this is not every user's schedule.
commands.safety: Read-only; inspect the correct account. System timers and /etc/cron* are separate sources.

commands.title: Time source tracking
commands.definition: Reports chrony's clock synchronization state and estimates.
commands.purpose: Investigate clock drift affecting authentication or logs.
commands.environment: Read-only; applies to hosts using chronyd and should be correlated with source status.
commands.interpretation: Reference ID names the source; System time and Last offset describe offsets. Leap status indicates synchronization condition.
commands.safety: Read-only; applies to hosts using chronyd and should be correlated with source status.

commands.title: Block device identifiers
commands.definition: Probes filesystem identifiers for a selected block device.
commands.purpose: Check UUID and filesystem type before editing mount configuration.
commands.environment: Read-only probe, often privileged; never infer that an unrecognized device is empty or safe to format.
commands.interpretation: UUID is filesystem identity; TYPE describes the detected format. Verify the physical/logical device selection separately.
commands.safety: Read-only probe, often privileged; never infer that an unrecognized device is empty or safe to format.

commands.title: Volume group capacity
commands.definition: Summarizes LVM volume groups and free physical capacity.
commands.purpose: Determine whether a logical volume can be extended within its group.
commands.environment: Read-only; requires LVM tooling and suitable device visibility.
commands.interpretation: VSize is group capacity and VFree is unallocated space; neither reports free filesystem bytes.
commands.safety: Read-only; requires LVM tooling and suitable device visibility.

commands.title: Logical volume layout
commands.definition: Displays logical volumes, attributes and backing devices.
commands.purpose: Map an application volume to underlying LVM storage.
commands.environment: Read-only; special layouts such as thin pools require additional capacity checks.
commands.interpretation: LSize is block volume capacity; Attr encodes volume properties. Filesystem growth is a separate concern.
commands.safety: Read-only; special layouts such as thin pools require additional capacity checks.

commands.title: Debian package inventory
commands.definition: Queries the installed Debian package database for a package version.
commands.purpose: Identify the package managed by the distribution before patch review.
commands.environment: Read-only; Debian/Ubuntu-family command. Check vendor advisories for security status.
commands.interpretation: Output contains package name and installed version; distribution backports mean upstream version alone may not establish vulnerability status.
commands.safety: Read-only; Debian/Ubuntu-family command. Check vendor advisories for security status.

commands.title: RPM package inventory
commands.definition: Queries the RPM database for an installed package.
commands.purpose: Check the distribution-managed package version on an RPM-based host.
commands.environment: Read-only; RPM-family system required. Vendor release metadata matters for backported fixes.
commands.interpretation: The returned name-version-release identifies the installed package; a not-installed result is distinct from an outdated version.
commands.safety: Read-only; RPM-family system required. Vendor release metadata matters for backported fixes.

commands.title: Effective sudo privileges
commands.definition: Lists sudo commands permitted for the current identity.
commands.purpose: Review practical privilege boundaries before administration or access changes.
commands.environment: Read-only privilege inspection but may prompt authentication and generate audit records. Do not assume a narrow command name means narrow impact.
commands.interpretation: Runas and command rules identify allowed operations; tools with shell escape or arbitrary-file features may grant broader capabilities.
commands.safety: Read-only privilege inspection but may prompt authentication and generate audit records. Do not assume a narrow command name means narrow impact.

debugging.title: Service fails after reboot
debugging.symptom: An application works after a manual start but is absent after reboot.

steps.evidence: Compare enabled state, unit dependencies and previous boot logs. A service may be static and activated by another unit rather than directly enabled.
Correct the intended activation relationship or enable the appropriate unit; fix missing storage/network prerequisites instead of adding arbitrary sleeps.
Test a controlled reboot or equivalent target activation and verify the application becomes ready without manual intervention.

references.title: Service fails after reboot — primary documentation

debugging.title: Bad unit override
debugging.symptom: A service stops starting after an override was added.

steps.evidence: Compare the base file and drop-ins with status and journal errors. Check command syntax, cleared/replaced directives and environment paths.
Correct the drop-in, reload unit definitions and restart only the affected service during a controlled window.
Confirm effective configuration, active state and a real application request; retain the previous override for rollback.

debugging.title: SSH change risks lockout
debugging.symptom: A new SSH configuration may prevent administrators from connecting.

steps.evidence: Validate syntax and inspect effective authentication and listen settings. Keep an existing session and independent recovery path available.
Correct invalid settings before reloading. Apply a scoped reload and test a second connection before closing the original session.
Confirm a fresh authorized login succeeds and disallowed authentication methods remain rejected.

references.title: SSH change risks lockout — primary documentation

debugging.title: Cron job works only manually
debugging.symptom: A script succeeds in a shell but fails on its schedule.

steps.evidence: For the actual scheduler, inspect logs, execution user, PATH, working directory and environment. Check overlap and permissions rather than assuming the script is identical at runtime.
Use explicit paths and environment, capture output and add appropriate locking or timeout behavior. Test under the scheduled identity.
Observe a scheduled run completing with the expected output and no overlapping duplicate work.

references.title: Cron job works only manually — primary documentation

debugging.title: Root disk fills with application data
debugging.symptom: The root filesystem fills even though the application normally writes to a separate data volume.

steps.evidence: Confirm whether the expected volume is actually mounted. A missing mount can leave an ordinary /data directory on root receiving writes.
Stop affected writers, preserve misplaced data, restore the correct mount and reconcile data carefully. Add a mount dependency to service startup.
Verify the source device, application data consistency and that new writes consume the intended filesystem.

debugging.title: Log rotation fails to reclaim space
debugging.symptom: Rotated logs disappear but storage remains full.

steps.evidence: Identify processes still writing to unlinked files and inspect the rotation policy's reopen action.
Use the application's supported reopen signal or controlled restart, then fix rotation integration. Avoid truncating unknown active files blindly.
Confirm free space recovers and new records appear in the current log after the next rotation.

references.title: Log rotation fails to reclaim space — primary documentation

debugging.title: Patch installed but process old
debugging.symptom: Package inventory shows a fixed version while a scanner still detects old running code.

steps.evidence: Compare process start time and mapped executable/library versions with the package update. Deleted mappings can indicate an old process image.
Restart affected services or reboot when required through a tested maintenance procedure; preserve availability during rolling updates.
Verify running versions and service health, then repeat the relevant detection check.

references.title: Patch installed but process old — primary documentation

debugging.title: Clock-related certificate failures
debugging.symptom: Several services report certificates not yet valid or expired at the same time.

steps.evidence: Compare host time with trusted sources and check synchronization status and offset. Separate a bad clock from genuinely expired certificates.
Restore the approved synchronization service and correct its source or connectivity. Consider application effects of large clock corrections.
Confirm time offset is acceptable and certificate checks succeed without disabling validation.

debugging.title: Backup restoration incomplete
debugging.symptom: A restored server boots but the application cannot serve requests.

steps.evidence: Check restored data age, credentials, encryption keys, DNS and dependency endpoints. Verify application-level consistency rather than only archive extraction.
Restore missing dependencies or data using the documented recovery order. Keep the restored environment isolated until correctness is established.
Execute representative reads and writes, compare recovered transactions with the RPO and record total recovery time against RTO.

debugging.title: Fleet rollout causes widespread errors
debugging.symptom: A configuration change starts failing on the first batch of hosts.

steps.evidence: Compare canary and unchanged hosts, rendered configuration and dependency behavior. Identify whether failure is host-specific or common to the change.
Stop further batches, roll back the affected cohort if compatible, and repair the configuration in source. Avoid concurrent manual edits across the fleet.
Verify canary recovery, rerun validation and resume only with healthy batch gates and sufficient capacity.

references.title: Fleet rollout causes widespread errors — primary documentation
